title: MENINTplus – Prospective Register Study on Meningitis and Encephalitis in Intensive Care Units in Germany
summary: A prospective, national registry on pathogen-related infections of the central nervous system (brain, spinal cord) in intensive care units in Germany is being established. A key focus of the register study is the systematic collection of clinical symptoms, examination findings, as well as laboratory and instrumental diagnostics in the initial phase of the disease. In addition, our study aims to systematically record the incidence of relevant complications and their respective treatment approaches, along with their impact on the prognosis of the specific infectious d. Furthermore, a follow-up survey of patients will capture the long-term course of the disease. Within the framework of the MENINT registry, information is documented by the study centers using a case report form forwarded to the study center at LMU Munich for evaluation.
conditions: Inflammatory diseases of the central nervous system

interventions.name: Patients with infections of the central nervous system who are treated in intensive care units in Germany.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Assignment to at least one of the following diagnostic groups possible:
- Bacterial CNS infection: Acute bacterial meningitis, subacute or chronic bacterial meningitis, bacterial brain abscess, nosocomial ventriculitis
- Viral CNS infections: Viral encephalitis caused by herpesviruses, viral encephalitis caused by flaviviruses, viral encephalitis caused by other viruses (only if pathogen detected)
- Fungal infections of the central nervous system
- Infections of the central nervous system with other pathogens (only if pathogen detected)
Exclusion criteria:
Age <18
No clear assignment of the diagnosis to the specified diagnosis groups possible
